summary: Backend regression + new-behavior verification for the driver↔zone bidirectional sync, auto-zone tagging on orders, zone-bucketed clustering with total_weight_kg, and the smarter capacity/license/zone/EV-aware auto-assignment. 47/47 pytest cases PASS (38 previous regression cases unchanged + 9 newly authored). No 500s, no tracebacks. The prior 38-test contract is fully preserved.
action_items: None blocking. Backend behaves exactly as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: services/zones.py::find_zone_for_point correctly returns the containing zone when the point is inside any polygon, else falls back to the nearest by centroid distance — verified by TestOrderZoneAutoTag (inside + outside cases).

services/clustering.py buckets by (zone_id, postal_sector) so a cluster cannot span two zones; total_weight_kg is rounded sum of member weights; zone_id is persisted on legacy orders that were missing it — all verified by TestClusteringByZone.

services/assignment.py enforces hard constraints (license matrix A=motorbike, B={motorbike,van}, C=van AND vehicle.capacity_kg ≥ cluster.total_weight_kg) and uses a scoring heuristic (zone bonus 1000, EV bonus 50, distance penalty 0.5/km, capacity-waste penalty 0.4/kg). Heaviest clusters processed first so they aren't stranded with motorbikes. Used drivers tracked in a set so the same driver is never assigned twice in one run. Skipped clusters are returned with a reason — verified by TestSmartAssignment.

routers/drivers.py POST adds driver to zones.driver_ids when zone_id provided; PUT pulls from old zone and addToSet to new zone only when the zone changes; DELETE pulls the driver from every zone's driver_ids — all three paths verified by TestDriverZoneSync.
routers/orders.py POST computes zone_id via find_zone_for_point before insert — verified by TestOrderZoneAutoTag.
Models: Cluster has total_weight_kg + zone_id; Order has zone_id; DriverIn has zone_id — all serialized correctly in API responses.

Minor robustness observation (not blocking): assign_clusters_to_drivers re-fetches the zone for each candidate inside _score_candidate (one DB hit per candidate per cluster). With many drivers this could be slow; caching zones in a dict at the start of the function would be a small optimisation. Not a correctness issue.
